figures.name: single_peak
figures.note: Reference set: one synaptic event, each profile with its own peak density (the densities of the earlier simulations).

figures.name: single_total
figures.note: Same as set 1, but every profile carries the same total CaLVA conductance on the dendrite, so differences come only from where the channels are. The hotspot is now denser than in set 1, the gradients peak at about 0.01 instead of 0.015 S/cm². The decreasing gradient, which places most of its channels on the proximal dendrite where synapses cannot trigger an event (Mechanism, sections 4 and 6), now produces no event at any site.

figures.name: train5x50Hz_peak
figures.note: Five events at 50 Hz. The Ca<sub>LVA</sub> event is triggered by the first input only; the later inputs find the channels inactivated (Mechanism, section 5), so the train mostly adds passive summation on top of the first event.

figures.name: single_peak_TTX_noSomaCa
figures.note: Na<sup>+</sup> channels blocked everywhere and somatic Ca<sub>LVA</sub> removed. The results are almost identical to set 1: the dendritic event does not depend on Na<sup>+</sup> channels or somatic Ca<sub>LVA</sub>.
